hook.line: Thirty-two octagonal pieces on a board with no river — still played in parks and homes all over Korea.
hook.say: Welcome to the story of janggi!

ch.say: Chinese chess was reborn on the Korean peninsula.
p: Chinese xiangqi reached the Korean peninsula and grew rules of its own. When it arrived is unclear.
The river went, the elephant and cannon changed, and the pieces became octagons.
st: Grows into janggi, with no river

ch.say: The rules changed little by little.
tl: Xiangqi with the cannon takes its modern form in China
The river disappears; the elephant and cannon change
Played in parks and homes, with tournaments

ch.say: The palace diagonals are a shortcut for everyone!
ch.cap: Pieces sit on the 9×10 points; no river, the X marks the palace
p: Pieces stand on the points and move along the lines.
The general and guards stay in the palace, whose diagonals chariots, cannons and soldiers may use too. The cannon always moves by jumping one piece.
